title: Born in Foggy Bottom, mother's Louisiana family, absent father
summary: Butler was born in Washington in 1909 in Foggy Bottom; his mother was from Lafayette, Louisiana (Lefebvre family, Negro and Indian mix) and he never really knew his father.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: : Do you recall -- we'd like to deal with your childhood now. When and where were you born and what do you know about your family line? That is, whether Indian, Scotch, Irish (inaudible)?

Well, I was born in Washington. The District of Columbia, it was called, in 1909. I was born in an area called Foggy Bottom. It was called Foggy Bottom because when they built Lincoln's tomb, they forgot -- neglected so that frogs (inaudible) and it seems that the river would overflow, you'd have Avenue A, B, C and D and E -- in fact, they were called streets, and in the wintertime -- A Street didn't exist. B Street didn't exist. It would come as far as C, and I lived on E. And the school was right across the street from me, Briggs School. My mother, she said that circumstances of being born was that I was born with a veil or enveloped and it seems that if you (inaudible), you are (inaudible).
My mother was a very, very, very wonderful person. She was from Lafayette, Louisiana. Her family name was

Lefebvre. This is a mixture of Negro and Indian, although I saw many blanché or fair-haired people coming up to visit us and they were kissing mother. So I would -- they was cousins or something of this sort.

My father, it seems, that I heard of him but I didn't see him until I was 50 years old and very rare occasion. It seems that my mother was working in service naturally for certain people who had the money and they fell in love or something happened there and I was created -- I happened on the scene. So as I can remember, my mother was telling me, "Your father is in Winston-Salem, North Carolina. You don't look like your father. You look like your uncle." So I kept that in mind. And then when I was about (inaudible), I remember vaguely that I must have been (unintelligible) something green in color above me and I was reaching up there, trying to get it.
